summary: Karl G. Heider studied at Williams College (~1952–1953), Harvard College (~1953–1956), and Harvard University (~1957–1966).

Karl H. Potter was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of California (~1947–1950) and Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and was a professor at the University of Minnesota (~1956–1970) and the University of Washington (~1970–1997).

Karl Hoffmann was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Ferdinand Sommer and Walther Wüst. He held chairs at Saarland University (1952–1955) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (1955–1983), and joined the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 1972.

Karl Jettmar studied at the University of Vienna (1936–1941), specializing in archaeology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and Indology. He held posts at Weltmuseum Wien, the University of Vienna, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, and was a director at Heidelberg University (1964–1986).

Karl Joseph Hieronymus Windischmann worked in philosophy and Indology, having studied at Mainz and Würzburg. He taught at Gymnasium Aschaffenburg and Karls-Universität Aschaffenburg from 1803, and was appointed professor in the medical faculty at the University of Bonn in 1818.

Karl Lachmann was a linguist who studied at the University of Leipzig (~1809–1812) and the University of Göttingen (~1812–1815). He held a post at the Humboldt University of Berlin from around 1825 to 1851.

Karl Marbe, who worked in linguistics and other fields, studied at the University of Bonn (~1891–1893). He held academic posts at the University of Würzburg (~1896–1935) and Goethe University Frankfurt (~1905–1909).

Karl Müllenhoff was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. After studying at Kiel, Berlin, and Leipzig, he held academic positions at Kiel University (from 1842) and Frederick William University Berlin (from 1858).

Karl Otfried Müller studied at Breslau and Berlin under August Boeckh, Friedrich Schleiermacher, and Friedrich August Wolf. A scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics, he taught at Magdalenaeum Wrocław and served as professor at the University of Göttingen from 1819.

Karl Popper was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vienna and the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Canterbury (1937–1945), the London School of Economics, King's College London, and the University of London (1949–1969).

Karl Richard Lepsius, an archaeologist, historian, and linguist, studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin. He held a chair at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1846–1884) and served as chief librarian at the Prussian State Library (~1873–1884).

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied under Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel at Berlin, Heidelberg, and Halle-Wittenberg. He held chairs of philosophy at the University of Halle (~1830–1833) and succeeded Johann Friedrich Herbart at the University of Königsberg in 1833.

Karl Verner was a linguist who studied at Aarhus Katedralskole, the University of Copenhagen, and under August Leskien. He worked as a librarian at Halle-Wittenberg (~1876–1883) and became a lecturer in Slavic studies at Copenhagen in 1882.
Karl von Hegel was a historian and archaeologist who held academic posts at the University of Rostock (~1841–1856) and the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1856–1888).

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying at Augsburg and the University of Munich, he held posts at Munich (1978–1988) and served as professor at the Technical University of Applied Sciences Würzburg-Schweinfurt (1992–2014).

Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist who earned his PhD at the University of Bonn and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He served as Privatdozent at Hamburg in 1999 and worked at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Karl-Heinz Gottmann was a Buddhist studies figure who studied as the primary student under Anagarika Govinda, whom he succeeded in 1982.

Karlfried Graf Dürckheim worked in religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kiel University (~1919–1923), he held posts at Leipzig (~1923–1930), Breslau (~1930–1932), Pädagogische Akademie Breslau, and the Bauhaus.
Karma Drubgyü Ngedön Nyingpo studied under Pema Wangchok Gyelpo and Khakyab Dorje.
Karma Lek Shé Drayang was a scholar who studied under Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.
